   "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: qpbt-full-speed-v2 -->\n## Motivation\n\nThe full speed run of 2026-09-12 (04:17Z\u201308:33Z) produced 9 merges and cost the owner\neight distinct classes of manual intervention, each of which is a defect of the workflow\n(`results/telemetry/owner-handoffs/2026-09-12-main.md`, the `## 2026-09-12` sections of the\nevent log, and the run summary). The owner had to restate the concurrency limits five\ntimes while ~90 worker sessions died (69 on a dead endpoint, the rest above an unmeasured\nprovider ceiling); ask repeatedly why slots were idle while every dispatched fixer was\ndying at a model-policy preflight; ask whether the project was progressing and then\ndictate the estimate format; ask why ready PRs were not merging; watch three lane-runner\nrevisions be hand-patched in `/tmp`; switch the speed tier three times by hand; and nudge\na main session whose message-delivery script auto-resumed the goal five minutes after the\nstop order.\n\nThe target state: the owner gives **one** briefing at the start of a run (keys and their\nlimits, duration or \"until my word\", speed tier, pause deadline) and afterwards receives\nonly the half-hourly one-line estimate on the estimate issue and prose progress on the\nprogress log. Everything else is an automatic mechanism, a one-file switch, or a\nself-healing loop, and every fix lives in the repository rather than in `/tmp`.\n\nDesign document: attached as the first comment on this issue, which is the brief of\nrecord; the per-item briefs land in `local/briefs/`.\n\n## Description\n\nSeven work items, disjoint file sets, each one reviewed PR closing one sub-issue of this\ntracker.\n\n1. **Owner briefing, run-mode and standing reports.** `local/bin/run_mode.py` validates\n   one `run-brief.json` and is the only writer of `watchdog/run-mode.json` and of the\n   derived cap files; `ready_report.py` answers \"ready but open, and why\" hourly on the\n   progress log; `estimate_post.py` is the single writer of the estimate issue and renders\n   exactly the two prescribed lines. The main persona gains a Standing reports section so\n   the closing report is a duty, not a pause-message dictation.\n2. **Dispatch and telemetry.** Provider failures are classified (`concurrency_limit`,\n   `endpoint_5xx`, `retries_exhausted`, `timeout`, `task_failure`, `unknown`) and recorded\n   with the endpoint, so a capacity refusal is no longer indistinguishable from a failed\n   proof; `dispatch.sh` spools its request and retries transient classes instead of dying\n   with its prompt; a branch claim stops two writers on one worktree; an owner model\n   override lives in the policy layer instead of a PATH-shim rewrite that made the session\n   registry record the wrong model; `autofix.sh` stops defaulting to a model its own\n   preflight rejects and gains the fix \u2192 CI \u2192 review loop that lived in `/tmp`.\n3. **Capacity controller.** An AIMD controller with per-endpoint health is the only writer\n   of the caps: it measures the real limit, trips to cap 0 on a 5xx endpoint, recovers\n   through a single half-open read-only probe, subtracts declared external consumers,\n   carries the measured limit into the next run, and fixes the pause/resume cap round-trip\n   (which today saves zeros and cannot be parsed back).\n4. **Operator-tools installer and owner controls.** One versioned installer deploys the\n   operator scripts with a hash manifest; +  "body": "### Motivation\n\nCloses #560. Every pause so far has been a hard landing: the 2026-09-12 chain killed\n17 codex sessions mid-work, and the 2026-09-14 fallout was reviewers that \"exited 143\",\nkill-caused `daemon/pr<N>.failed` markers that made the merge daemon skip PRs for two\nhours, and lanes restarted from scratch on heads that already carried a green CI and a\nfinished review. A codex session has already paid for its input and its reasoning, so a\nkill throws that away and the resume pays again.\n\nStacked on `issue-550-full-speed-v2` (PR #552), like #554 and #556.\n\n### Description\n\n**Two owner words.** `owner-pause.sh --cutoff` stops admission and nothing else \u2014 caps to\n0 through run-mode, `watchdog/drain`, no signal, no daemon stopped \u2014 and may be given long\nbefore the pause. `owner-pause.sh` (no flag) is the pause word and starts the deadline from\n`run.pause_deadline_min`. A pause without a prior cutoff degrades to the landing rule.\n\n**Age-based landing.** At the pause word `local/bin/pause_landing.py` classifies every live\ncodex session from the spool and `/proc`: young sessions (under `young_max_min`) stop at\nonce, a mature reviewer runs to the last call and is then restarted from scratch, and a\nmature writer is checkpointed \u2014 worktree untouched, thread id, worktree, step and elapsed\ntime recorded \u2014 and stopped only at the last call. Every threshold lives in\n`local/capacity-policy.json`; no number is written into a shell script.\n\n**Pause manifest.** `watchdog/pause-state.json` gains a `landing` key: the resolved\nthresholds, each lane with its issue, branch, head, the step it reached, its head's\nstatuses and its own environment, each stopped session with thread id, role, worktree,\nelapsed time and resumability, and the `daemon/pr<N>.failed` markers the pause caused,\nrecorded by difference against a snapshot taken at T+0:00.\n\n**Resuming the work.** `owner-resume.sh` replays that manifest after its post-condition\ncheck: each parked lane at the step it reached (no merge/build/push on an unchanged head,\nno CI when `local-ci/summary` is already success, no review when `local-review/summary` is,\nnothing at all when both are), each checkpointed writer the lane does not own on its own\ncodex thread through `dispatch.sh --resume`, each stopped reviewer from scratch, and each\nrecorded marker cleared.\n\n**Prover milestone rule.** The prover dispatch prompt and `local/personas/prover.md` carry\n\"commit each proved lemma in the worktree, with the hooks running, before starting the\nnext one\", and the continue prompt tells a resumed prover to read its worktree and continue\nfrom that state. A kill then costs at most the work since the last commit.\n\n### Review findings and how each was addressed\n\nTwo independent reviews produced 33 findings (9 blockers, 13 major, 7 minor, 4 nits; several\nwere reported by both reviews). All are addressed; none is disputed.\n\n**Blockers**\n\n| Finding | Addressed |\n|---|---|\n| `resume_plan` emits a parked lane AND the session that lane owns: two writers in one worktree, a merge and a build in a tree codex is editing, a branch claim the loser dies 5 on | `lane_owned()`: a lane owns every session in its worktree or on its branch. Only the lane is relaunched, and `lane.sh` resumes the thread from `<state>/<issue>.thread`; the session is listed as owned, with argv `None`. Test: `test_a_lane_and_its_own_worker_are_never_both_launched`, whose fixture puts lane 7 and `prover-7-a` on one worktree |\n| `lane_resume_step` falls through to `publish`, so a lane killed mid-work publishes a half-finished worktree through PR, CI and review | `publish` only for a lane that reached publication (recorded step `publish`/`ci`/`review`); `warm` and `dispatch` resume at `dispatch`, which reuses the lane's thread record. Tests: `test_a_lane_stopped_before_publication_resumes_at_dispatch`, `test_a_lane_that_reached_publication_resumes_at_publish` |\n| The resume is not idempotent: a second `owner-resume.sh` relaunches every lane and every session again | `resume-exec` stamps `landing.replayed_at` plus one `replay` row per item; `resume-plan`/`resume-exec` then emit nothing without `--force`. Test: `test_a_replayed_manifest_launches_nothing_a_second_time` |\n| The post-condition requires `watchdog/paused`, which nothing ever creates, so the whole work-resume block was unreachable after a real pause | `stop_admission` writes `$W/paused` next to `$W/drain`. Tests: `test_the_pause_writes_every_marker_the_resume_requires` (every marker the post-condition requires must be one the pause writes) and an end-to-end `owner-pause.sh --cutoff` against a scratch cache root |\n| The landing signals the `dispatch.sh` wrapper, not codex: its TERM trap is deferred while the `codex \\| tee` pipeline is in the foreground, so codex keeps spending quota and the SIGKILL skips `cleanup()` | `terminate()` signals the recorded pid **and** its process tree (`Processes.ppid` + `descendants`), which ends codex and lets the wrapper's own TERM trap and `cleanup` run; after a SIGKILL, `free_locks()` releases the account slot, the branch claim and the spool row explicitly. Tests: `test_the_codex_child_is_signalled_with_its_dispatcher`, `test_a_killed_wrapper_has_its_slot_claim_and_spool_row_freed`, `test_a_session_that_stops_on_term_keeps_its_locks` |\n| The grace is slept once per session, so a phase costs `grace_s x sessions` and runs past the deadline | `land()` is two passes: one SIGTERM pass, ONE sleep, then SIGKILL to the survivors. Test: `test_the_grace_is_slept_once_for_the_phase_not_once_per_session` (17 sessions, `slept == [grace_s]`) |\n| The resume dispatch drops the job class, effort, hardness reason, persona, sandbox and account, so `account_router` refuses the resume with \"resume cannot switch model\" and nothing is relaunched | `RESUME_FIELD_FLAGS` carries `--job-class`, `--effort`, `--hardness-reason`, `--account`, the recorded `--sandbox`, and `--persona`/`--persona-ref` when the recorded label has the `<ref>:<path>` shape it was built from. Tests: `test_a_checkpointed_prover_is_resumed_on_its_own_thread`, `test_the_sandbox_is_the_one_the_session_was_dispatched_with` |\n\n**Major**\n\n| Finding | Addressed |\n|---|---|\n| The recycled-pid guard is not fail-closed: an unreadable cmdline is signalled unverified, and any `dispatch.sh` cmdline satisfies it for any record | `is_ours()`: an empty command line is `not-ours`, `dispatch.sh` is necessary and never sufficient, and the recorded name, worktree or `--role <r> --issue <i>` pair must appear. Tests: `test_an_unreadable_command_line_is_spared_not_signalled`, `test_a_different_dispatch_on_a_recycled_pid_is_not_ours`, `test_the_recorded_worktree_identifies_a_real_dispatcher` |\n| `failed_markers` is always empty: the snapshot is taken ten minutes after the only process that writes such a marker was stopped | New `markers` subcommand, called at T+0:00 before the daemon-stop phase; `manifest` keeps an existing snapshot. Tests: `test_the_marker_snapshot_is_taken_before_the_daemon_is_stopped`, `test_a_second_manifest_keeps_the_first_landings_record` |\n| The lane relaunch drops `LANE_BRANCH`, `SKIP_REVIEW`, `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_CMD` | `live_lanes` reads `/proc/<pid>/environ` and records them; `LANE_BRANCH` also decides the recorded branch and worktree, and `lane_env()` re-emits them. Test: `test_a_lanes_own_environment_is_recorded_with_it` |\n| A checkpointed writer whose thread id was not captured is stopped and then silently never put back | It gets a fresh `dispatch.sh` with `RESTART_PROMPT` (read the worktree, continue from that state); a session that genuinely cannot be rebuilt is printed as `STOPPED AND NOT PUT BACK`. Tests: `test_a_writer_without_a_thread_id_gets_a_fresh_session_not_silence`, `test_a_session_that_cannot_be_rebuilt_is_named_loudly` |\n| A failed landing phase is invisible because the pipeline's status comes from `sed`, and the last call is not a superset | `land_phase()` checks `PIPESTATUS[0]`; `land --phase last` stops everything still `pending`, whatever its recorded action. Tests: `test_a_failed_landing_phase_is_not_swallowed_by_the_pipe`, `test_the_last_call_also_stops_a_row_an_earlier_phase_missed` |\n| After a `--cutoff`, the pause word records the already-zeroed caps | The caps come from `saved_caps` (then `derived.caps`); the live-file readers are skipped while a cutoff is in force; `write_state` refuses to lower an already-recorded nonzero cap to zero. Test: `test_the_relaunch_argv_is_one_the_next_pause_can_still_see`, which checks the argv against both `LANE_RE` and the sweep's own patterns |\n\n**Minor**\n\n| Finding | Addressed |\n|---|---|\n| A head carrying a finished review re-runs the review | `lane_env()` adds `SKIP_REVIEW=1` when `local-review/summary` is success on the unchanged head. Test: `test_a_pending_ci_resumes_at_ci_and_skips_the_finished_review` |\n| Running the pause twice destroys the first landing's record | `merge_manifest()` keeps every row the first landing stopped and the earliest `markers_before` |\n| One failed launch aborts the rest of the resume plan | Each launch is guarded; the row records `FAILED to launch: \u2026`, the plan continues, and the command exits 4 with a summary. `owner-resume.sh` treats 4 as a partial replay, not a total failure. Test: `test_one_failed_launch_does_not_cost_the_rest_of_the_plan` |\n| The `last_call_s` shell fallback is 60 while the policy and the module say 90 | Changed to 90, and `test_every_shell_fallback_equals_the_modules_default` now asserts every `pl_get KEY fallback` literal against `pause_landing.DEFAULTS` |\n| `watchdog/cutoff` is never cleared, so every cutoff after the first is silent | `owner-resume.sh` removes it, and a marker older than `cutoff_lead_min` is re-asserted with a fresh message.    "body": "### Motivation\n\nThe full speed run of 2026-09-12 (04:17Z\u201308:33Z) produced 9 merges and cost the owner\neight distinct classes of manual intervention, each of which is a defect of the workflow\nrather than of the mathematics: the concurrency limits restated five times while ~90\nworker sessions died (69 on an endpoint that had been answering 503 for an hour, the rest\nabove an unmeasured provider ceiling); repeated questions about idle slots while every\ndispatched fixer was dying at a model-policy preflight; the estimate format dictated by\nhand after multi-line prose appeared on the estimate issue; ready PRs sitting open behind\ntwo-hour timer backoffs; three lane-runner revisions hand-patched in `/tmp`; the speed\ntier switched three times by string surgery on a generated file; and a terminal stop order\nundone five minutes later by a goal keeper that had no way to know about it.\n\nThis PR is the whole of the tracker's seven work items: the owner gives **one** briefing at\nthe start of a run and afterwards receives only the half-hourly one-line estimate and prose\nprogress on the progress log. Everything else becomes an automatic mechanism, a one-file\nswitch or a self-healing loop, and every fix that lived in `/tmp` or in one host's\n`.git/config` now lives in the repository. The design document is the first comment on\n#550.\n\n### Description\n\n**1. Owner briefing, run mode and standing reports.** `local/bin/run_mode.py` validates one\n`run-brief.json` and is the single writer of `watchdog/run-mode.json` and of the derived cap\nfiles, and the single accessor for every capacity, schedule, speed and issue number, so no\nprotocol, persona or script carries a literal that can go stale. `ready_report.py` answers\n\"ready but open, and why\" hourly from daemon state, with `unexplained` as the alarm case.\n`estimate_post.py` renders the two prescribed lines and refuses any other body.\n`local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md` is the runbook and `local/personas/main.md` gains the\nStanding reports duty.\n\n**2. Dispatch and telemetry.** Provider failures are classified (`concurrency_limit`,\n`endpoint_5xx`, `retries_exhausted`, `timeout`, `task_failure`, `unknown`) and recorded with\nthe endpoint, so a capacity refusal is no longer scored like a failed proof; `dispatch.sh`\nspools its request and prompt and retries a transient class instead of dying; a branch claim\nrefuses a second writer with exit 5; the owner model override moves from a PATH-shim rewrite\n(which made the registry record a model that never ran) into the policy layer; `autofix.sh`\nstops defaulting to a model its own preflight rejects and gains the fix \u2192 CI \u2192 review loop.\n\n**3. Capacity controller.** An AIMD controller with per-endpoint health is the only writer of\nthe caps: it measures the real limit under the briefed ceiling, trips to cap 0 on a 5xx\nendpoint, recovers through one half-open read-only probe, subtracts declared external\nconsumers, and carries the measurement into the next run.\n\n**4. Operator tools.** One versioned installer with a hash manifest that refuses to overwrite\na hand patch; one `owner-pause.sh` whose every phase is clamped to the briefed deadline and\nwhich releases queued dispatches rather than killing them; one `owner-resume.sh` that\nrestores from the recorded state only; one `owner-say.sh` whose terminal mode holds the goal\nbefore it speaks.\n\n**5. Merge daemon and lane runner, promoted.** Honest names in the repository, failure markers\nthat carry a class and clear on an observable change instead of a timer, PAR sized from the\nmachine, the lane's build under the machine-wide lease, a retirement pass \u2014 and the lane's\n`MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` fallback push deleted.\n\n**6. Self-repair janitor.** One idempotent sweep of five passes, each selecting by record\nfield: no date glob and no filename digit filter anywhere.\n\n**7. Merge hygiene and build reachability.** A committed `.gitattributes` union driver for the\nappend-only logs, asserted by `worktree-setup.sh`; and a reachability guard inside the\nexisting `local-ci/build` step that names a module left outside the umbrella import closure.\n\n**No proof-integrity mechanism is touched.** No change to `.githooks/*`,\n`merge_loss_guard.py`, `checked-push.sh`, the seven `pr_merge.py` gates, the eight canonical\n`local-ci/<step>` contexts or the review-verdict contract. The one place a current tool\n*bypassed* a gate \u2014 the lane's hook-skipping fallback push \u2014 is removed, which strengthens it.\n\n### Testing\n\nRun in the branch worktree on the build host.\n\n- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` \u2192 **977 tests, OK**\n  (9 skipped: the historical useful-queue scenarios retired by #505). That is the command the\n  pre-commit hook runs, and it ran on every commit here that stages a `scripts/` file.\n- `bash -n` on all 24 changed shell files and both renderings of the generated PATH shim: clean.\n- `python3 -m py_compile` on all 26 changed Python files: clean. `json.load` on\n  `model-policy.json`, `capacity-pol\n\n---\nCloses #550\n",

+## Findings
+
+- [ ] F1 (blocker) `local/bin/pause_landing.py:896` — A new pause retains stopped sessions from the previously replayed pause while dropping its replay stamp, causing old work to be launched again.
+- [ ] F2 (blocker) `local/bin/pause_landing.py:421` — The live-session snapshot drops resume-critical spool fields, allowing model-mismatched resumes, sandbox escalation, and taskless fresh restarts.
+- [ ] F3 (changes) `local/bin/pause_landing.py:902` — An empty pre-pause marker snapshot is treated as absent and replaced later, hiding kill-created failure markers in the common no-existing-marker case.
+- [ ] F4 (changes) `results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-pause.sh:594` — Failure markers are collected before the lane sweep, while surviving review and refresh wrappers can publish interruption failures afterward.
+- [ ] F5 (changes) `local/bin/pause_landing.py:643` — Every marker changed after the snapshot is classified as landing-created, so legitimate pause-window failures are deleted on resume.
+- [ ] F6 (changes) `local/bin/pause_landing.py:500` — Lane progress is inferred from persistent per-issue logs that `lane.sh` does not clear, allowing stale evidence to skip unfinished work.
+- [ ] F7 (changes) `local/bin/pause_landing.py:596` — Lane discovery bypasses the registry-first worktree resolver and therefore records the wrong head for valid nonstandard worktrees.
+- [ ] F8 (changes) `results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-pause.sh:619` — The last-call path sleeps one grace period inside `land` and another during the sweep, contradicting the one-grace deadline contract.
+- [ ] F9 (changes) `local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md:286` — The protocol amendment lacks the mandatory trigger event and corresponding `EVOLUTION.md` entry.
+
+## Review
+
+**F1:** `owner-resume.sh` leaves the replayed manifest in `pause-state.json`. A later pause preserves it, and `merge_manifest` carries forward every previously signalled session but initializes from the fresh document, losing `replayed_at`. The next resume consequently plans those old sessions again. A reproduced merge retained the old `KILL` row and generated a new dispatch for it. A pause episode identifier or explicit reset after replay is required.
+
+**F2:** `dispatch.sh` records `sandbox`, `job_class`, `effort`, `hardness_reason`, `persona`, `persona_ref`, and `prompt_file`, but `live_sessions` discards all of them. `session_command` later assumes they survived. This can trigger `account_router.py`’s “resume cannot switch model” check, restart a read-only role with `workspace-write`, or create a fresh session without its original task. The tests hide this by constructing resume manifests containing these fields manually.
+
+**F3:** `{}` is a valid marker snapshot meaning no failures existed at T+0. Both `merge_manifest` and the CLI use truthiness, so that snapshot is discarded and retaken at landing time. Any marker created during the pause is then considered pre-existing and cannot be cleared.
+
+**F4:** `land --phase last` records `failed_markers` before the subsequent anchored sweep. Killing a refresh lane can make its surviving merge-daemon wrapper write `pr<N>.failed` afterward. The sweep also omits `review.sh`, so killing only its nested dispatcher lets the wrapper publish failure or partial review evidence while resume schedules a fresh review.
+
+**F5:** Mtime difference establishes chronology, not causality. The merge daemon remains active for the first 30 seconds, and detached work can fail naturally later. Those legitimate structured failure records are currently marked `created_by_landing` and unlinked.
+
+**F6:** A new lane removes only `.done` and `.needs-attention`; old `.dispatch.log`, `.ci.log`, `.review.log`, and `.pr.md` files remain. A pause during a new warm, dispatch, merge, or build phase can therefore classify it as `review`, or even `done` when its old head still has green statuses.
+
+**F7:** `lane.sh` explicitly resolves worktrees from Git’s registry before considering `.worktrees/<branch>`. The manifest instead invents that conventional path. For a registered worktree elsewhere, the recorded head becomes null and resume unnecessarily restarts from dispatch rather than using the recorded stage.
+
+**F8:** `land()` sleeps `grace_s` after terminating classified sessions; the shell then unconditionally sleeps `GRACE_S` again. The default last-call-to-publish interval is only 30 seconds, and collapsed deadlines necessarily overrun.
+
+**F9:** `local/protocols/meta.md` requires every protocol edit to ship with an evidence trigger and `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` amendment. Neither is present in this diff.
+

/-!
# Combined lines and restricted line distributions

This module states the construction of the joint X/Z line measurements, the
mixture and error-inflation estimates for restricted line distributions, and
the sub-line distribution used to combine the two bases.  The extended line
in the sub-line construction uses the directly indexed carrier, so the
sub-line statement is a formalization auxiliary assertion and carries no
divisibility hypothesis at dimension `2 * m + 2`.

## References

The declarations formalize `lem:qld-xz-lines` and
`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; `exists_subLineWitness`
instead supports `lem:qld-sublines` through the directly indexed extended-line
carrier and probability law.  Their paper sources
are `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:882-894`
and `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1069`.
-/

`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They
are read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`
gate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add
locking there.

The parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that
a CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice
(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale
build; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.

Both locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with
the same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on
what a stale lock is.

### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`

`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two
compatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:

* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,
  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to
  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override
  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the
  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the
  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,
  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see
  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)
* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO
  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.
  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude "no pid, therefore
  stale" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here
  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then
  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`
  field is read as "this host", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.

---

## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`

Replaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s
GitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:

1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a
   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable
   error.
2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is
   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.
3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only
   if the pin is not already installed.
4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).
5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every
   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the
   documented failure this check exists to surface.
6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).
7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the
   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed
   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.
   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).
   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the
   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol
   exists to prevent.
8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`
   calls out `--check` specifically for *"each fresh worktree used for a PR."*

`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero
if anything is missing.

### 8.1 Git environment hygiene

Every invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in
`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every
variable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a
script invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into
Lake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.

### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround

Kept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a
pristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.

*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib
post-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before
fetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not
exist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create
the directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.

*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is
**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.
Recorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed
by a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts

# --only run can never leave the review gate a green status it did not earn.
PARTIAL=0
if [ -n "$ONLY_STEPS" ] || [ "$SKIP_BUILD" = 1 ] || [ -n "$BASE_OVERRIDE" ]; then
  # --base is in this list because an overridden base (the PR head, say) can
  # empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success (round 2 F1; round 3 F1
  # caught this line resetting the earlier fix).
  PARTIAL=1
fi
# The manifest is runtime evidence, not a record: GitHub carries the verdict
# (statuses + the manifest comment), the cache carries the raw JSON next to
# the step logs it references.
MANIFEST_DIR="$CACHE_ROOT/ci-manifests"
if [ "$PARTIAL" = 1 ]; then
  MANIFEST="$MANIFEST_DIR/pr$PR_ID-$HEAD_SHA.partial.json"
else

fi
STEPS_TSV="$RUN_TMP/steps.tsv"
WARN_FILE="$RUN_TMP/warnings.txt"
: > "$STEPS_TSV"
: > "$WARN_FILE"

sanitize_field() {
  printf '%s' "$1" | tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | cut -c1-500
}

record_step() {
  # name outcome seconds log blocking note
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
    "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5" "$(sanitize_field "${6:-}")" >> "$STEPS_TSV"
}

SHORT_SHA="$(git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse --short "$HEAD_SHA")"
info "PR $PR_ID  branch $BRANCH  head $SHORT_SHA  base $BASE_REF"
info "worktree $WORKTREE"
info "changed files: $(wc -l < "$CHANGED_FILES" | tr -d ' ')"
info "areas: lean=$A_lean mip_lean=$A_mip_lean ldt_lean=$A_ldt_lean blueprint=$A_blueprint blueprint_src=$A_blueprint_src tex_chapter=$A_tex_chapter paper_gaps=$A_paper_gaps scripts=$A_scripts comparator=$A_comparator workflow=$A_workflow"

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
  info "dry run: planned steps"
  for _step in $STEP_NAMES; do

    if [ "$FORCE_ALL" = 1 ] || step_gate "$_step"; then _plan="run"; fi
    if [ -n "$ONLY_STEPS" ]; then
      case " $ONLY_STEPS " in
        *" $_step "*) ;;

    fi
    if [ "$_step" = build ] && [ "$SKIP_BUILD" = 1 ]; then _plan="skip (--skip-build)"; fi

if ! acquire_lock "$PR_LOCK" 0 "$BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S" "ci.sh pr=$PR_ID sha=$HEAD_SHA"; then

note_warning() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$WARN_FILE"; printf 'WARNING: %s\n' "$*"; }

step_build() {

  # is the only writer of the shared snapshot; this worktree gets a private
  # copy-on-write clone (DESIGN.md invariant 1).
  if [ ! -d .lake/build ]; then
    if [ -x "$SCRIPT_DIR/warm-worktree.sh" ]; then
      echo "+ warm-worktree.sh $WORKTREE"
      if ! "$SCRIPT_DIR/warm-worktree.sh" "$WORKTREE"; then

      fi
    elif [ "${MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER:-}" = "1" ]; then
      printf 'ERROR: %s is missing and MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1.\n' "$SCRIPT_DIR/warm-worktree.sh"

    fi

  require_tool lake "install elan (https://github.com/leanprover/elan) and re-run"

  # Two-tier cache, do not conflate (gotcha 1): .lake/build holds this
  # project's oleans and is per-worktree; .lake/packages holds Mathlib and

  # tree and must be treated as read-only: `lake exe cache get` writes there.
  if [ -L .lake/packages ]; then

    printf 'Bootstrap the worktree first (local/bin/worktree-setup.sh), which also carries\n'
    printf 'the ProofWidgets prune workaround that only bites on package-free trees.\n'

    record_step "$STEP" skipped 0 "$LOG" 1 "no changes under $(step_gate_paths "$STEP")"
    printf '  %-18s skipped\n' "$STEP"
    continue
  fi

  if [ "$STEP" = build ] && [ "$SKIP_BUILD" = 1 ]; then
    record_step "$STEP" skipped 0 "$LOG" 1 "operator passed --skip-build"
    printf '  %-18s skipped (--skip-build)\n' "$STEP"
    continue
  fi

  : > "$LOG"
  _step_start="$(epoch_now)"

  # Invariant 7: at most one full lake build machine-wide.  Only the build
  # step compiles; the audits are pure Python and take no lock.
  _locked=1
  if [ "$STEP" = build ]; then
    if acquire_lock "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK" "$BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S" "$BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S" "ci.sh pr=$PR_ID sha=$HEAD_SHA"; then
      _locked=0
    else
      _locked=2
    fi
  else
    _locked=0
  fi

  if [ "$_locked" = 2 ]; then
    {
      printf 'ERROR: could not take the machine-wide full-build lock %s within %ss.\n' "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK" "$BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S"

    # code, releases the build lock, and continues with independent steps.
    ( set -e; run_step_body "$STEP" ) >> "$LOG" 2>&1
    _rc=$?
    set -e
    if [ "$STEP" = build ]; then
      release_lock "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK"
    fi
  fi

  _elapsed=$(( $(epoch_now) - _step_start ))

  if [ "$_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    _outcome=success
    _note=""

    _outcome=error
    _note="step could not run: $(grep -m1 '^ERROR:' "$LOG" 2>/dev/null || echo 'missing tool or prerequisite')"

    _outcome=failure
    _note="exit $_rc"

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  # checked-push sets an expected tuple when only the expensive gate is skipped.
  if [ -n "${MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE:-}" ]; then
    if ! IFS= read -r ACTUAL_PUSH_TUPLE; then
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checked ref is already current."
      exit 0
    fi
    if IFS= read -r EXTRA_PUSH_TUPLE; then
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: expected exactly one advertised ref tuple." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$ACTUAL_PUSH_TUPLE" != "$MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE" ]; then
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: advertised ref tuple changed after preflight." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: confirmed preflight ref tuple."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push hook skipped by MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1."
  exit 0
fi

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"

CHANGED_FILE_LIST="$(mktemp)"
CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST"' EXIT
BLUEPRINT_WEB_SMOKE_RAN=0

ZERO_SHA="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"

run_outside_git_env() (
  for name in $(git rev-parse --local-env-vars); do
    unset "$name"
  done
  "$@"
)

lean_file_to_module() {
  path="${1%.lean}"
  printf '%s\n' "$path" | tr '/' '.'
}

while read LOCAL_REF LOCAL_SHA REMOTE_REF REMOTE_SHA
do
  if [ -z "${LOCAL_SHA:-}" ] || [ "$LOCAL_SHA" = "$ZERO_SHA" ]; then
    continue
  fi

  if [ "$REMOTE_SHA" = "$ZERO_SHA" ]; then
    if git rev-parse --verify origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      BASE_SHA="$(git merge-base "$LOCAL_SHA" origin/main)"
    else
      BASE_SHA="$(git rev-list --max-parents=0 "$LOCAL_SHA" | tail -n 1)"
    fi
  else
    BASE_SHA="$REMOTE_SHA"
  fi

  git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR "$BASE_SHA" "$LOCAL_SHA" -- >> "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"
done

sort -u "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" -o "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"
grep -E '^(MIPStarRE/.*\.lean|MIPStarRE\.lean)$' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" \
  > "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST" || true

if [ ! -s "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: no changed tracked files detected."
  exit 0
fi

if [ -s "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checking changed Lean files."
  while read LEAN_FILE
    do
      if [ -f "$LEAN_FILE" ]; then
        echo "  lake env lean $LEAN_FILE"
        run_outside_git_env lake env lean "$LEAN_FILE"
      fi
    done < "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST"
fi

if [ -s "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST" ] ||
    grep -Eq '^scripts/(check_oversized_lean_files\.py|tests/test_check_oversized_lean_files\.py)$' \
      "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checking Lean file length guard."
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/check_oversized_lean_files.py --root .
fi

if grep -Eq '^(MIPStarRE/LDT/.*\.lean|MIPStarRE/LDT\.lean|MIPStarRE\.lean)$' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"; then
  if grep -Fxq 'MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: axiom audit already checked as a changed Lean file."
  else
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checking LDT axiom audit."
    run_outside_git_env lake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean
  fi
fi

if grep -Eq '^(MIPStarRE/|MIPStarRE\.lean$|blueprint/src/|blueprint/lean_decls|scripts/(audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata|audit_paper_facing_proof_debt|audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses|audit_unfaithful_markers|audit_lean_axiom_declarations|check_paper_gap_note_style|check_statement_paper_origin|check_source_statement_changes|blueprint_lean_sync|lean_header_utils)\.py|docs/(CONTRIBUTING|project_conventions|anti_patterns|blueprint_style_guide|formalization-patterns|proof_frontier_review)\.md|docs/paper-gaps/|\.github/(actions|prompts|workflows)/|AGENTS\.md)' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checking statement-integrity audits."
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: do not close proof gaps by adding non-paper bridge/package hypotheses."
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/check_paper_gap_note_style.py \
    --root . \
    --changed-files-file "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" \
    --ci
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/check_statement_paper_origin.py --root .
  if git rev-parse --verify origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [ -s "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST" ]; then
      run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata.py \
        --root . \
        --base origin/main \
        --changed-files $(cat "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST") \
        --ci
    else
      run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata.py \
        --root . \
        --base origin/main \
        --changed-files \
        --ci
    fi
  else
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: origin/main not found; skipping new proof-obligation metadata guard."
  fi
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py --root . --ci
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --root . --ci
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/audit_unfaithful_markers.py --root . --ci
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py --root . --ci
fi

if [ -s "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST" ]; then
  if git rev-parse --verify origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checking source-labelled statement headers."
    run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/check_source_statement_changes.py \
      --root . \
      --base origin/main \
      --changed-files $(cat "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST")
  else
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: origin/main not found; skipping source statement header guard."
  fi
fi

if grep -Eq '^blueprint/src/' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"; then
  if ! command -v leanblueprint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: blueprint/src changed, but leanblueprint is not on PATH."
    echo "Install it with:"
    echo "  pipx install leanblueprint"
    echo "  pipx inject --include-apps --force leanblueprint plastex"
    echo "Or bypass only for a local tooling problem with MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1 and let CI run."
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: running blueprint web smoke check."
  run_outside_git_env sh -c 'cd blueprint && leanblueprint web'
  BLUEPRINT_WEB_SMOKE_RAN=1
fi

if grep -Eq '^(blueprint/src/|scripts/(check_blueprint_latex|tex_utils)\.py$)' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checking blueprint LaTeX conventions."
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/check_blueprint_latex.py --root blueprint/src
fi

if grep -Eq '^(MIPStarRE/|MIPStarRE\.lean$|blueprint/|scripts/(blueprint_lean_sync|blueprint_leanok_axioms|check_blueprint_latex|check_blueprint_sync|tex_utils)\.py$)' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: regenerating blueprint/lean_decls."
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py --root . --update-lean-decls
  if ! git diff --quiet -- blueprint/lean_decls; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: blueprint/lean_decls changed; stage and commit it before pushing."
    git diff -- blueprint/lean_decls
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checking blueprint and Lean declaration sync."
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py --root . --ci
  if [ -s "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST" ]; then
    if git rev-parse --verify origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: warning on changed Lean declarations missing blueprint tags."
      run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py \
        --root . \
        --warn-missing-blueprint \
        --diff-base origin/main \
        --changed-files $(cat "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST")
    else
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: origin/main not found; skipping reverse blueprint coverage warning."
    fi

    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: refreshing compiled Lean modules for checkdecls."
    while read LEAN_FILE
      do
        if [ -f "$LEAN_FILE" ]; then
          LEAN_MODULE="$(lean_file_to_module "$LEAN_FILE")"
          echo "  lake build $LEAN_MODULE"
          run_outside_git_env lake build "$LEAN_MODULE"
        fi
      done < "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST"
  fi
  run_outside_git_env lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls
fi

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_HOOK_FULL:-}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push full mode: running lake build."
  run_outside_git_env lake build

  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push full mode: checking blueprint proof-level leanok closure."
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci

  if [ "$BLUEPRINT_WEB_SMOKE_RAN" = "1" ]; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push full mode: blueprint web already checked."
  elif command -v leanblueprint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push full mode: running leanblueprint web."
    run_outside_git_env sh -c 'cd blueprint && leanblueprint web'
  else
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push full mode: leanblueprint not found; skipping web build."
  fi
fi

echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: ok."

 "body": "## Motivation\n\nStage 4.3 proof packet for issue #436 (see the issue body for targets, sources and plan).\n\n## Description\n\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-436-diagonal-zero-direction-mass\n- chore(telemetry): Opus assistance window 2026-09-14 (rounds 1-6, repairs, space-1 key retired)\n- chore(telemetry): GitHub record snapshot\n- chore(telemetry): records around PR 361 merge\n- Merge pull request #361 from Dengnifer/issue-360-supplied-direct-soundness\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-360-supplied-direct-soundness\n- docs(blueprint): record zero-direction line-point mass support\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-436-diagonal-zero-direction-mass\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-360-supplied-direct-soundness\n- fix(QPBT/Combining): withdraw supplied-witness wrapper for review F1\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-436-diagonal-zero-direction-mass\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-360-supplied-direct-soundness\n- merge github/main into issue-436-diagonal-zero-direction-mass\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-360-supplied-direct-soundness\n- feat(QPBT/Combining): bound diagonal zero-direction mass\n- Merge repaired passing-value dependency\n- Merge refreshed direct soundness dependency\n- Add supplied-witness direct soundness\n- Merge direct any-strategy soundness dependency\n- Merge ground-slice compression into any-strategy soundness\n- feat(QPBT/Combining): transport direct soundness through Naimark\n\n## Testing\n\nWorker checked every changed file with `lake env lean`; exact-head CI and review follow.\n\n---\nCloses #436\n",

item.aggregated_output:
# Build cache protocol — the hot main cache

Normative. This document specifies the local replacement for the parent
workflow's GitHub Actions build cache, and the rules every worktree must obey to
avoid duplicate compilation. It is the protocol behind three executables:

| script | role |
|---|---|
| `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh` | the **single writer**: builds `main`, publishes read-only snapshots |
| `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` | the **consumer**: keyhash-gated copy-on-write clone into a worktree |
| `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` | fresh-worktree bootstrap (replaces `.codex/setup.sh`) |

Governing invariants: `local/DESIGN.md` #1 (single cache writer) and #7 (one full
`lake build` machine-wide). Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,
`DESIGN.md` wins.

---

## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way

The parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented
failure. The load-bearing citations:

| parent mechanism | citation | what it encodes |
|---|---|---|
| Split restore/save, save only on `main` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:137-167` | *"The cache is saved only from main and restored everywhere."* |
| `lean-action`'s own cache disabled | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:138-142` | The post-mortem: a ~2.6 GB entry saved **per PR run** cycled through the 10 GB repository cache budget and evicted the main-branch entry, *"so no run ever restored usable MIPStarRE oleans and every run rebuilt the whole library."* |
| Same policy restated in the weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget."* |
| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache."* |
| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile."* |
| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |
| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could negate the ProofWidgets workaround"* |
| Independent cache for the doc subproject | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:135-140` | `docbuild/` is its own Lake project with its own key |
| Mathlib bumps are manual only | `.github/workflows/update.yml:3-5` | A bump *"triggers a full library rebuild and possibly an auto-fix cascade"* |
| Lean setup removed from a PR job | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *"after repeated runner disk exhaustion"* |

The single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable
cache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the
same failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared
build tree.

---

## 2. The two-tier split

`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and
different sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the
parent's failure.

An absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` relocates `.lake` to `<root>/<branch>` for a
one-component branch name. The helper rejects `/`, symlink targets, escape, and
canonical overlap with packages, `hot-main`, the repository, or any worktree,
plus canonical-equal ownership by another worktree. Export it before setup or
warming and through dispatch and cleanup; only its target gets `--add-dir`.

**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,
`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the
parent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and
distributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**
copy.

**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The
parent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud
cache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once
per manifest** in a shared, read-only store:
`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,
and every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.

> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a
> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it
> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any
> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest
> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by
> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old
> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches
> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,
> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key
> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).
> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.

Consequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It
rewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under
every published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib
bumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.

---

## 3. The cache key

```
keyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )
```

concatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local
analog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in
`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`
and `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay
byte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.
A missing input file is a hard error, never a default.

Two properties matter, and they are not symmetric:

1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's
   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest
   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is
   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash
   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not
   need their timestamps preserved.
2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,
   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.
   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`
   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls
   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.

---

## 4. On-disk layout

Shared packages and `hot-main` use `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`; branch products may
use `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` as in §2. Neither runtime tree is committed.

```
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/
├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time
│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose
├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends
├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)
└── hot-main/
    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this
    │   └── info
    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main
    ├── snapshots/
    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
    │   │   ├── STAMP
    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build
    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink
```

Snapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse
lexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`
calls and no name parsing.

### `STAMP` schema

A flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts
parse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase
hex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever
`eval`ed or `source`d.

```
sha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>
keyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>
timestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>
timestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>
status=complete|partial
build_seconds=<integer>
toolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>
snapshot=<snapshot directory name>
warmer_version=1
```

---

## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`

```
local/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]
                          [--targets "<lake targets>"] [--lock-timeout S]
                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]
```

### 5.1 Writer lease

Acquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic
test-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,
`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.

Staleness is decided in this order:

* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead
  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.
* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).

The TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this
repository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,
2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease
mid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to
prevent.

**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that
both judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;
`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and
re-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A
`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.

### 5.2 Build

1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`
   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.
   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and
   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).
2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).
3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**
   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and
   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,
   finish, then warm again.
4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply
   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.
   **No `lake update`.**
5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.
   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is
   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent
   prompts may later read.

### 5.3 Atomic publish

The publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:

1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with
   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the
   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).
2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.
3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.
   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already
   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**
4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over
   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).

> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,
> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would
> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real
> trap, not a hypothetical one.

Consumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the
resolved concrete path for the rest of the run.

## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate

| lock | path | held by | protects |
|---|---|---|---|
| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |
| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |

They are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the
warmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease
does not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.

`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They
are read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`
gate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add
locking there.

The parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that
a CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice
(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale
build; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.

Both locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with
the same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on
what a stale lock is.

### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`

`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two
compatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:

* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,
  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to
  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override
  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the
  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the
  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,
  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see
  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)
* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO
  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.
  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude "no pid, therefore
  stale" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here
  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then
  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`
  field is read as "this host", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.

---

## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`

Replaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s
GitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:

1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a
   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable
   error.
2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is
   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.
3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only
   if the pin is not already installed.
4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).
5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every
   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the
   documented failure this check exists to surface.
6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).
7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the
   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed
   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.
   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).
   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the
   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol
   exists to prevent.
8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`
   calls out `--check` specifically for *"each fresh worktree used for a PR."*

`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero
if anything is missing.
